source_documents.title: Naphthalimide Derivatives with Extended Heterocyclic Systems—Synthesis, Spectral and Sensing Properties

conditions_studied: solution: DMF 1e-5 M and other solvents
titrations with acid and metal ions

reference_evidence_units.quote: The reference compound 3a emits blue fluorescence with an intense maximum at 414 nm and a quantum yield of 27%.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3a
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bright blue emission without a receptor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The receptor-containing analogue 3b displays an emission band of identical shape and position but with significantly reduced intensity
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3b

reference_evidence_units.quote: The pronounced fluorescence suppression without any change in emission wavelength is a clear indication of an operative reductive PET process from the dimethylamino receptor to the excited NI chromophore, effectively quenching the fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3b
reference_evidence_units.statement: Quenching without a spectral shift is assigned to PET from the receptor amine.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The difference between the energy of orbitals of the receptor (HOMO) and the one of the chromophore (HOMO-1) is 0.3 eV, suggesting that, when excitation occurs, an electron would be transferred from the receptor to the fluorophore, which will lead to the quenching of 3b emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3b
reference_evidence_units.statement: The receptor HOMO lies 0.3 eV above the chromophore HOMO-1, allowing PET.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Fluorescence titration experiments confirmed that the receptor-bearing benzofuranannulated NI functions as a switch-ON PET sensor for protons and selected metal cations, with pronounced responses toward Cu(II) and Sn(II).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3b + H+ or metal ions
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonation or metal binding restores the emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Needs a proton or metal ion, not in the input.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Both symmetrically benzofuran-annulated imides 3 exhibit a broad, structured absorption band in the 325–400 nm region, which can be assigned to a π–π* transition within the extended aromatic system.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3a, 3b
reference_evidence_units.statement: π-π* chromophore with small Stokes shift.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This electronic arrangement is manifested by a broad, structureless absorption band in the blue region, with a maximum at 417 nm, which can be assigned to an intramolecular charge-transfer (ICT) transition (Figure 2a).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 13a, 13b
reference_evidence_units.statement: Benzodioxin-annulated NIs have an ICT band at 417 nm.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, benzodioxin-annulated derivatives exhibit broad, structureless absorption bands assigned to intramolecular charge-transfer transitions and inherently low fluorescence quantum yields in polar media, accompanied by large Stokes shifts.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 13a, 13b
reference_evidence_units.statement: ICT character with large Stokes shift and low QY (13b 2.1%, 13a 5.2%).

reference_evidence_units.quote: In these systems, the receptor orbital is located energetically below the chromophore HOMO (Figure 5), which prevents photoinduced electron transfer and explains the negligible PET effect in these compounds.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 13b
reference_evidence_units.statement: No PET driving force in the benzodioxin series.

contrast_group.varied_factor: imide N substituent on the benzofuran-annulated naphthalimide (2,6-diisopropylphenyl vs 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl receptor)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The amine receptor quenches the emission by PET (QY 26.9% to 4.9%, same band); protons or metal ions switch it back on.

basis: same benzofuran-annulated chromophore as 3b (SI name, OPSIN) with the N-(2,6-diisopropylphenyl) imide named in the main text (Scheme 1)
